LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 THE PUNCTUATION THE COMMA AND DOUBLE QUESTION MARKS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 The Punctuation The comma and Double Question Marks
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 The Punctuation The comma and Double Question Marks, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we punctuate our speech or writing correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the comma and double quotation marks in braille/print text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.4.1 The Punctuation The comma and Double Question Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use the comma and the double quotation marks correctly in oral and braille/print written text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.4.1 The Punctuation The comma and Double Question Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. collaborate with peers to determine the correctness featuring the comma and the double quotation marks. ● In groups, learner is guided to identify sentences in which the comma and the double quotation marks have been used ● Learners are guided to recite a poem while paying attention to the use of the comma and the double quotation marks. ● In groups, learners are guided to listen to an oral presentation and answer questions. ● Learner is guided to form sentences from a substitution table. ● In groups, learners are guided to construct a few sentences, punctuate them correctly, create a braille/print poster with appropriate font size and colour contrast and exchange the work to another group for peer 1) Why should we punctuate our speech or writing correctly? 2) How can we use commas, double quotation marks to punctuate written sentences 45 correction. ● Learner is guided to listen to a dictation of sentences, write the sentences and punctuate them appropriately. correctly?

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.4.1 The Punctuation The comma and Double Question Marks in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.4.1 The Punctuation The comma and Double Question Marks together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
